result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers cover every style in a scannable table with rem sizes and unitless line heights, and both flag the title tightening, label tracking and tabular figures as values to confirm. A is stronger on link states, with hover, visited and focus written out in CSS, and on narrow and wide screens, with balanced wrapping, a 65ch line-length cap and tests at 320px and 200% zoom. A also leaves the colors as placeholders. B invents hex values (marked to confirm) and says only that one set of sizes applies at all breakpoints. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers cover every style in clear tables, with rem sizes and unitless line heights. B goes further on behaviour across screen sizes: text-wrap, a 65ch measure, a 320px test and zoom checks. It also gives full CSS for all link states and uses placeholders for colors instead of inventing hex values. A flags its made-up hex values for confirmation, but it says less about responsive behaviour and does not clearly mark the label tracking as adjustable.
